newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Japan patrols remove protest flags from islands.
newsitem.headline: Japan patrols remove protest flags from islands.

text.p: Japanese maritime police removed the flags of Taiwan and China from an East China Sea archipelago early on Monday soon after protesters raised them to challenge Japan's sovereignty claim, Taiwan Television said.

"After our side raised the two flags, Japanese police pulled them down immediately," a reporter said from a protest flotilla that mounted a brazen landing on the islands claimed by Japan as the Senkakus and known in Taiwan and China as the Diaoyus.

Dozens of Japanese patrol boats and helicopters blared out advisories for the 50 Taiwan protest vessels to leave what they called Japan territory as police scrambled ashore to pursue four activists who managed to reach the uninhabited islands, the television station said.

The activists had pledged to remove Japan's national flag and pull down a lighthouse erected by Japanese right extremists in July in a move that triggered anti-Japanese protests among Chinese in Taiwan, Hong Kong, Macau and China.
It was not immediately known whether the four protesters, from Taiwan and Hong Kong, had reached the lighthouse.
There was no estimate of how many Japanese police had gone ashore to pursue the landing party.
